note: What a server sends to put a turret on the field. In everything observed it arrives only inside EnterSight, and the channel and delivery recorded here are those of the message carrying it. The header names the unit this is about.

fields.name: turret
fields.note: The name the turret answers to, so later messages can name it.

fields.name: node
fields.note: Which network node the object belongs to. A client reads it apart from the name beside it rather than as that name's leading byte.

fields.name: name
fields.note: What this turret is called, so a client can tell one from another. Written out in full and padded with zero bytes to the width above.

bits.name: targetable
bits.note: A client reads it and does nothing with it: a turret's targetability comes by replication.

bits.name: unused
bits.note: A client does not read these.

fields.name: targetableBy
fields.note: Who may target the turret. A client reads it and does nothing with it; the same value by replication compares whole: 8388608 not its own side, 16777216 not the other side, 25165824 nobody, 33554432 everyone, anything else both sides.

revisions.note: A client matches name exactly against the map's turrets. With no match it only removes any object holding the id; a matched turret missing or dead is rebuilt before it takes the id.

fields.name: turret
fields.note: The name the turret answers to, so later messages can name it.

fields.name: node
fields.note: Which network node the object belongs to. A client reads it apart from the name beside it rather than as that name's leading byte.

fields.name: name
fields.note: What this turret is called, so a client can tell one from another. Written out in full and padded with zero bytes to the width above.

bits.name: targetable
bits.note: Set where anything may aim at it.

fields.name: targetableBy
fields.note: Which sides may aim at it. The bits within are undetermined.
